hook: What an *API* actually is, explained without the jargon

points.title: A menu for software
points.body: An API lists what a program can do for you, and how to ask.

points.title: You send a request
points.body: Your app asks for something specific, like a user's profile or today's orders.

points.title: You get a response
points.body: The other system replies with data, usually as JSON, or an error explaining why.

caption:
APIs sound complicated until you picture them as a menu.
Request in, response out. That is the whole idea.
What should I break down next? 👇

hook: Next.js just shipped a *critical* remote code fix

points.title: RCE in next/og ImageResponse
points.body: Versions 16.2.0 to 16.3.5 have a remote code execution flaw in Satori's SVG output.

points.title: Edge runtime and 15.x untouched
points.body: Only the Node.js ImageResponse implementation in next/og is vulnerable to this issue.

points.title: Fix now
points.body: Upgrade to 16.3.6 now; 15.5.26 adds related hardening, both are already live.

caption:
Critical RCE patched in Next.js next/og.
Update before shipping anything new.

hook: Over 16,000 *Supabase* databases have publicly readable tables

points.title: AI tools create tables with RLS off
points.body: The dashboard turns RLS on by default. Raw SQL migrations, common in AI tools, don't.

visual.title: migration.sql
visual.code:
-- written by an AI tool
create table public.orders (
  id uuid primary key,
  user_id uuid,
  email text
);
-- RLS is off unless you enable it

points.title: Turn RLS on for every table
points.body: One line per table. With RLS on and no policy, nobody gets rows.

visual.title: enable_rls.sql
visual.code:
alter table public.orders
  enable row level security;

points.title: Add a policy matching rows to users
points.body: Each user should read only their own rows. Never use true for anon.

visual.title: policy.sql
visual.code:
create policy "Own rows only"
on public.orders for select
to authenticated
using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );

cta: Is *RLS* on for every table you ship?
caption:
UpGuard found 16,326 Supabase databases with publicly readable tables.
Many come down to missing row level security, one line of SQL per table.
Did your last AI-built app ship with RLS on? 👇
voiceover: [urgent] Sixteen thousand Supabase databases are exposing data. (break) [deadpan] Many from one missing line.
[knowing] The dashboard switches security on for you. [exasperated] AI writing raw SQL? Security's off.
[confident and fast] One line fixes it per table. [excited] Turn on row level security, and nobody reads anything.
[serious, fast] Add a policy: users see only their own rows. [emphasis] Never write one that just says true.
[warm, curious] Be honest, (break) [teasing] is row level security on for all your tables?

hook: Claude Code silently *ignored* your AGENTS.md file

points.title: A remote flag gated the feature
points.body: AGENTS.md only loaded if a hidden flag was on, tied to telemetry.

points.title: It failed silently, no warning shown
points.body: Privacy-minded devs who disabled telemetry got no error, just ignored instructions.

points.title: Anthropic fixed it within days
points.body: The flag was decoupled from telemetry, and the mod's source was published.

cta: Do you actually *verify* your agent reads its rules?
caption:
Claude Code quietly skipped your AGENTS.md file.
If telemetry was off, so were your instructions.
Do you check what your AI tool actually reads? 👇
voiceover: [urgent] Your coding agent might ignore the file steering it.
[serious, fast] It added a rules file, gated behind a hidden switch. (break) [urgent] That switch only turned on with telemetry.
[knowing] So if you turned telemetry off for privacy, (break) [exasperated] your instructions just vanished, with no warning at all.
[confident and fast] Anthropic fixed it within days, (break) [amused] and even published the code for anyone to check.
[warm, curious] Do you ever check what your tools actually read?
